title: Quantitative assessment of bone density changes in spontaneously healing mandibular lesions
html: This study quantified bone mineral density (BMD) of regenerated bone in mandibular cystic defects following enucleation using quantitative computed tomography. A retrospective analysis was conducted on 126 computed tomography scans from 81 patients to measure BMD during bone healing. Linear mixed models and Spearman’s rank-order correlation were applied to investigate associations between BMD and patient age, gender, cavity size, condylar BMD, and cavity healing percentage. Regenerated bone BMD increased significantly during the first six months postoperatively, with median values of 245 mg/cm3 at 3 months and 326 mg/cm3 at 6 months, after which the rate of increase slowed.
